Going back to my first computer, an 8086 with a 1200 baud modem that could only connect to modems of the same brand at 1200 (Otherwise all other modems connected at 900.)

Anyways bulletin board systems had what they called "Door Games" The first "door game" I remember playing was a top down one square playing field. Everybody had a little square with a line coming out of it (It was a square tank). You moved your tank around the obstacles and tried to take out the other tanks. At 1200 baud modem everybody could manage to play this with the same slowness to it worked very well. For those less interested in visual games. MUDs (Multi-User Dungeons) existed on these sites as well. It would tell you things like "You are in a room, there is a door to your right and a desk with drawers to your left, what would you like to do" you say "Go Left" and it says "You begin looking through the desk, you find a.... Letter Opener". Now you have your first weapon and can "Go right" "You have left the room and entered a dark hallway", etc.

I'll go ahead and move up to the early/mid 90s. Hayes-Compatiable had come out and people could 14.4K with the best of them. This opened up BBS's from "door games" To what they called Game Connection. IT basically allowed up to 4 (More?) players to connect to games like Doom or Doom II. As long as everybody downloaded the same map from the BBS File system everybody could load it and play these games across the Game Connection network.
